1: Trinity, which is above every being and goodness — guide us to the mystic summits of thy words, where the unsearchable and unseeable and unknowable things are veiled. And thou, my friend, practise the entrance into the darkness of unknowing, leaving behind all things that the senses and the mind can grasp.

The Blessed One said: and he said it while ascending — that God is not in the likeness of anything, nor is there any figure of Him. And the prophet went into the darkness, and from the darkness he spoke, and what he spoke we do not know — and that is the whole of the theology.

So we say of Him: He is not soul, nor mind, nor imagination, nor opinion, nor reason, nor understanding. He is not number, nor order, nor greatness, nor smallness. He is not light, nor darkness; He is not error, nor truth. And every name we give Him is a door; and He is beyond every door.
2: [Mystical Theology, ch. 4 — The darkness of light]

And the superessential ray of the divine darkness shines most brightly in the darkest night, and the invisible and unspeakable beauty is most radiant in the blindness of the eyes that are closed to all things — for only the blinded eye sees the light that is beyond light.

He is the hyper-being, the hyper-good, the hyper-God: above every affirmation, for every affirmation falls short; above every negation, for negation is a kind of saying. And He is celebrated by the removal of all things, as a sculptor removes the stone until the hidden form appears.
[Mystical Theology, ch. 5 — The end of the words]

And now, having said all that may be said, let us close the words. For the theology of the hidden God is finished when the speaking is finished, and the soul stands alone before Him, and He is not what the soul says, nor what the soul does not say — and the standing is the prayer.
